title: ICSE CLASS 6 — Science | Motion Measurement
description: Subject-wise test on Motion Measurement (Science) for ICSE CLASS 6. 25Q.
subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the following is the standard unit of length in the International System of Units (SI)?

options.explanation: Centimetre is a derived unit of length in the SI system.
Kilometre is a derived unit of length in the SI system.
The metre is the fundamental unit of length in the SI system.
Millimetre is a derived unit of length in the SI system.

questions.explanation: The metre is the fundamental unit of length in the SI system, from which other units like centimetre, kilometre, and millimetre are derived.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: When an object moves along a straight line, its motion is called:

options.explanation: Circular motion is along a circle.
Rectilinear motion describes movement along a straight path.
Periodic motion repeats after a fixed interval.
Rotational motion is spinning around an axis.

questions.explanation: Rectilinear motion describes movement along a straight path.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the following would be the most appropriate device to measure the length of a piece of cloth?

options.explanation: Foot spans are non-standard units and are inaccurate.
Handspans are non-standard units and are inaccurate.
While a metre scale is accurate, it may not be as practical for measuring cloth as a tailor's measuring tape.
A tailor's measuring tape is flexible and long, making it most practical and accurate for measuring lengths of cloth.

questions.explanation: A tailor's measuring tape is flexible and long, making it most practical and accurate for measuring lengths of cloth.

questions.question: A car travels a distance of 180 kilometres in 3 hours. What is its average speed?

Speed = 180 km / 3 hours = 60 km/h, not 50 km/h.
Speed = 180 km / 3 hours = 60 km/h.
Speed = 180 km / 3 hours = 60 km/h, not 90 km/h.

questions.question: Which of these motions is an example of periodic motion?

options.text: A car moving on a straight road.
options.explanation: A car on a straight road is rectilinear, not periodic.

options.text: A child sliding down a slide.
options.explanation: Sliding down a slide is rectilinear, not periodic.
The pendulum of a clock swings back and forth, repeating its motion regularly.
A spinning top is rotational, not periodic.

questions.explanation: Periodic motion is motion that repeats itself after a fixed interval of time.

questions.question: The motion of a potter's wheel is an example of __________ motion.

options.explanation: Rectilinear motion is along a straight line.
Periodic motion repeats after a fixed interval.
A potter's wheel spins around a fixed axis.
Oscillatory motion is back and forth around a point.

options.explanation: The tip of a minute hand exhibits both circular and periodic motion.
The tip of a minute hand exhibits both circular and periodic motion.

questions.question: While measuring the length of an object with a ruler, you should always place the ruler such that its zero mark:

options.text: Is slightly before the starting point of the object.
options.explanation: The zero mark must be placed precisely at the starting point.

options.text: Coincides exactly with the starting point of the object.

options.text: Is slightly after the starting point of the object.
options.explanation: The zero mark must be placed precisely at the starting point.

questions.question: Which of the following is the standard unit (SI unit) for measuring length?

options.explanation: Centimeter is a unit of length, but it is not the standard unit (SI unit) for measuring length.
The meter is the standard unit (SI unit) for measuring length.
Kilometer is a unit of length, but it is not the standard unit (SI unit) for measuring length.
Millimeter is a unit of length, but it is not the standard unit (SI unit) for measuring length.

questions.explanation: The International System of Units (SI) defines the meter as the standard unit for measuring length, used globally for consistency.

questions.question: When an object changes its position with respect to its surroundings over a period of time, it is said to be in:

options.explanation: Rest is the state of an object when it is not changing its position.
Motion is the change in position of an object relative to a reference point over time.
Equilibrium is the state of an object when the net force acting on it is zero.
Standstill is the state of an object when it is not moving.

questions.explanation: Motion is defined as the change in position of an object relative to a reference point over time.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: The back-and-forth movement of a swing is an example of which type of motion?

options.explanation: Rectilinear motion is a type of motion in a straight line.
Circular motion is a type of motion in a circular path.
Oscillatory motion is a repetitive back-and-forth movement about a central or mean position.
Rotational motion is a type of motion in which an object rotates around a fixed axis.

questions.explanation: Oscillatory motion is a repetitive back-and-forth movement about a central or mean position, which perfectly describes a swing.

questions.question: Which instrument would you use to accurately measure the length of a piece of fabric that is several meters long?

options.explanation: A measuring tape is flexible and typically much longer than a ruler.
A ruler is not typically long enough to measure several meters of fabric.
A divider is not typically used to measure length.
A set square is not typically used to measure length.

questions.explanation: A measuring tape is flexible and typically much longer than a ruler, making it suitable for accurately measuring extended or curved lengths of fabric.

questions.question: A train moving on a straight railway track exhibits ______ motion, while the blades of a rotating fan exhibit ______ motion.

options.explanation: The train exhibits rectilinear motion, not circular motion.
The train exhibits rectilinear motion, and the fan blades exhibit circular motion.
The train exhibits rectilinear motion, not oscillatory motion.
The fan blades exhibit circular motion, not oscillatory motion.

questions.question: A student wants to measure the distance covered by an ant crawling along a meandering path on the floor. Which of the following methods would provide the most accurate measurement?

options.text: Using a short ruler to measure segments of the path and adding them up.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary function of the root system in most plants?

options.explanation: The roots do not produce food for the plant, this is done by the leaves through photosynthesis.
The roots do not help the plant breathe, this is done by the leaves through stomata.

options.text: To absorb water and minerals from the soil
options.explanation: The roots are responsible for absorbing water and minerals from the soil.

options.text: To support the flowers and fruits
options.explanation: The roots do not directly support the flowers and fruits, this is done by the stem.

questions.question: Which part of a plant is primarily responsible for the process of photosynthesis?

options.explanation: The stem does not carry out photosynthesis, it transports water and nutrients.
The flower does not carry out photosynthesis, it is involved in reproduction.
The leaf is responsible for photosynthesis.
The root does not carry out photosynthesis, it absorbs water and nutrients.

questions.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll and specialized cells that capture sunlight and carry out photosynthesis to produce food for the plant.

questions.question: A gardener observes two different plants. Plant A has a single main root with smaller side roots branching off, while Plant B has a cluster of thin, bushy roots originating from the base of the stem. Which statement correctly identifies their root systems?

options.text: Plant A has a fibrous root system, and Plant B has a taproot system.
options.explanation: This is the opposite of the correct identification.

options.text: Plant A has a taproot system, and Plant B has a fibrous root system.
options.explanation: This is the correct identification based on the description.

options.text: Both Plant A and Plant B have taproot systems.
options.explanation: Plant B does not have a taproot system, it has a fibrous root system.

options.text: Both Plant A and Plant B have fibrous root systems.
options.explanation: Plant A does not have a fibrous root system, it has a taproot system.

questions.question: Rohan noticed that his potted plant started wilting, even though the soil was moist. He also observed that the stem of the plant felt soft and was bending. Which crucial function of the stem is most likely affected in this situation?

options.explanation: The stem does store food, but this is not the primary function affected in this situation.
The production of flowers is not directly related to the symptoms described.
The symptoms described indicate a problem with the conduction of water and minerals.
The anchorage of the plant is not directly related to the symptoms described.

questions.explanation: The stem's primary function includes conducting water and minerals from the roots to the leaves. Wilting and a soft, bending stem indicate that water is not being transported effectively, leading to a loss of turgor and support.

questions.question: A botanist discovers a new plant species. He observes that its leaves have a network-like (reticulate) venation pattern, and its flowers have petals in multiples of five. Based on these characteristics, what can he most likely infer about its root system?

options.text: It has a fibrous root system.
options.explanation: The characteristics described are more typical of a dicotyledonous plant, which usually has a taproot system.
The characteristics described are typical of a dicotyledonous plant, which usually has a taproot system.

options.text: It has aerial roots that grow above the ground.
options.explanation: There is no indication that the plant has aerial roots.

options.text: It does not possess a well-developed root system.
options.explanation: There is no indication that the plant lacks a well-developed root system.

questions.explanation: Plants with reticulate (net-like) venation in their leaves and flowers with petals in multiples of four or five are typically dicotyledonous plants. Dicotyledonous plants are generally characterized by having a taproot system.
